Four rows, two of each kind. The two niche rows are the two `Option`s; the two wrapper rows are `Arc` (3 fields, only slot 0 non-ZST) and `NonNull` (1 field), and WITHOUT them the derived path's `extractfield struct.0 %1, 0` in `Arc::deref` has no aggregate to extract from -- the heap holds one pointer WORD. A field counts as a ZST only when its own `StructDef.size` is `Some(0)`, measured, never inferred from a name; a struct with two non-ZST fields is REFUSED rather than having one of them picked. `first_named_by`/`table`/`decl` record WHICH artifact answered each row, because the raw aggregate ids COLLIDE across the two merged artifacts -- the crate module's `enum.1` is `InductiveError` and the sidecar's is `Option<Arc<Level>>` -- and every row here resolved through the sidecar (`merge@5617`), which its `decl` names. The refusal beside them is recorded too: `Level` itself is niche-encoded (5 variants, niched 0..3 from 3, `Param` untagged at 4) and `IREnc.nicheptr` is two-variant only, so no row is derivable for it and none is invented.
